title: Dynamic circuit breakers for tiered routing with hysteresis and request-throttling triggers
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design and implement a dynamic circuit breaker subsystem for the smart routing layer that automatically triggers fallbacks (to alternate region, lower-cost tiers, or smaller model variants) when service-level signals indicate degraded capacity or quality. Triggers should include sustained 429 spikes, tail-latency/timeouts, elevated error-rate, and saturation of KV cache or GPU queues. The system must include hysteresis to avoid oscillation, request-throttling and gradual backoff, and per-route/per-customer tunables exposed to Console. Integration points: routing policy engine, fallback model catalog, Dedicated capacity signals, and Console observability/rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Circuit breaker evaluates 429-rate, p95 latency, and 5xx error rate on a 1m rolling window and can open/close based on configurable thresholds
When circuit opens, routing engine routes >=95% of new requests for affected route to configured fallback tier/model within 30s
Hysteresis prevents flip-flopping: circuit requires sustained healthy signals for 3 consecutive windows before closing
Fallback preserves session affinity for chat where possible and preserves/re-syncs KV cache metadata with minimal token duplication
Feature is behind a feature flag and can be canaried to selected customers/routes via Console
Automated tests and chaos-run simulate 429 bursts and timeouts; post-deploy dashboards show expected behavior
implementation_notes: Use EWMA on error/latency counts to smooth short spikes and avoid aggressive tripping
Maintain per-route circuit state in Redis with TTL + version to support multi-region control plane
Support two circuit types: fast (20s window) for latency/timeout spikes, and slow (5m window) for sustained error-rate/429s
Expose three configurable actions on open: ROUTE_FALLBACK_MODEL, ROUTE_REGION_FAILOVER, THROTTLE_WITH_503 or combination
Include soft-fallback mode that preserves original routing but slows traffic via token-based request-throttling
Integrate with quota accounting to ensure cost attribution when falling back to higher-cost variants
rollout_plan: Canary: enable for 5% of routes (non-critical customers) for 24h and validate metrics
Staged ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% over 2 weeks with manual approval gates
Enable per-customer override in Console for enterprise customers during canary
Final global enabling tied to runtime-1.22 release window and post-deploy verification
testing_plan: Unit tests for EWMA threshold logic and hysteresis state transitions
Integration test: inject synthetic 429 burst from upstream and validate fallback routing within SLA
Chaos test: kill backend pool to induce timeouts and verify graceful degradation and no data loss
E2E: validate KV cache rehydration after fallback/return-to-primary flows
Load test: ensure circuit state store scales to 50k active routes without hotspotting
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: per-route circuit state, open-rate, time-in-open, and fallback traffic fraction
SLO alerts: if >1% of routes open for >10m, page oncall
Anomaly detection: sudden increase in hysteresis-reopen counts -> investigate flapping
Cost alert: fallback to higher-cost variants exceeding budget thresholds triggers ops notification
